artworks.title: Telethusa and Iphis Pray to Isis
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum Ovid print: Telethusa and Iphis kneel before Isis — the Cretan mother's prayer that will change her daughter's sex on the wedding morning.

artworks.title: Telethusa and Iphis Pray to Isis
artworks.description: Another Metamorphoses plate of the same prayer — Telethusa as the mother who dared Isis rather than expose the infant.

artworks.title: Isis and Iphis
artworks.description: Baur's Ovid illustration: Isis answering the Cretan household — Telethusa's goddess intervening in Iphis' fate.

artworks.title: Isis Changes Iphis into a Man
artworks.description: Theatrical Ovid print of the transformation Telethusa prayed for — Isis' answer the morning Iphis was to marry Ianthe.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IX — Telethusa saves Iphis by raising her as a boy, then prays Isis for the change that makes the wedding true.

popCulture.title: Telethusa
popCulture.description: Cretan mother of Iphis — Ovid's heroine of maternal cunning and Isis' miracle.
